descriptive_title: Grade 1 Mathematics: Demonstrations — A First Look at Likelihood (D2.1-D2.2)
short_description: A 5-day Grade 1 unit on likelihood framed around Lucky Lou the Loon and Maybe Mae the Cat. Children learn IMPOSSIBLE, POSSIBLE, CERTAIN, predict outcomes, and test predictions in another group.
long_description: Open the Likelihood Lab! This 5-day Ontario-aligned Grade 1 unit covers both D2 expectations (D2.1, D2.2) through a friendly detective frame with Lucky Lou the Loon and Maybe Mae the Cat. Day 1 introduces IMPOSSIBLE, POSSIBLE, CERTAIN through silly + everyday events. Day 2 sorts 24 events into 3 likelihood buckets. Day 3 introduces PREDICT and uses likelihood to predict coin flips, dice rolls, and marble pulls. Day 4 introduces TEST and predicts across two groups (home vs school). Day 5 closes with a 5-station Likelihood Lab capstone. Includes 5 lesson plans with expanded walkthroughs (each tackling a specific Grade-1 trap: all-possible default, silly-not-impossible, perfectionist after wrong predictions, prediction-stuck across groups, post-hoc prediction), 5 student worksheets, 12 paper manipulatives (event cards, sort mat, paper coins, paper dice, prediction mat, capstone template, anchor charts, outcome cards, poster, two character puppets), a mid-unit formative check, end-of-unit reflection sheet, class diagnostic checklist, three formative trackers, a 2-row summative rubric on Ontario's 4-level scale, a summative task script, and Junior Likelihood Detective certificates. Pedagogical approach: hands-on probability with Canadian context (loonies, hockey, snow), structured pair work, and a clear predict-test-report cycle.
